CausalChain: HCC cells secrete exosomal PKM2 -> Exosomal PKM2 is internalized by macrophage precursors/Kupffer cells -> Upregulation of PFKFB3 enhances glycolysis -> Increased glycolytic flux leads to PD-L1 upregulation and M2 polarization -> Hypoxia-induced lactate accumulation and Wnt signaling further reinforce M2 state -> Immunosuppressive TAMs inhibit CD8+ T cell function -> Blocking PKM2/PFKFB3 axis reprograms TAMs to M1 -> Enhanced CD8+ T cell activity improves tumor control
Hypothesis: Targeting the exosomal PKM2–PFKFB3 axis in HCC, while concurrently accounting for the hypoxia-driven lactate environment and additional modulatory pathways such as Wnt signaling, will reprogram tumor-associated macrophages from a pro-tumoral M2 phenotype to an antitumoral M1 state. Utilizing precision nanocarriers to deliver PKM2 inhibitors or siRNA and PFKFB3 modulators directly into TAMs will reduce glycolysis-induced PD-L1 expression, thereby restoring CD8+ T cell activity and enhancing responses to immune checkpoint blockade. This multifaceted approach leverages advanced targeting technologies to address both the metabolic and immune suppressive aspects of the HCC tumor microenvironment.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression is strongly influenced by the crosstalk between tumor cells and the immune microenvironment, particularly via tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs). Our revised hypothesis posits that the exosomal PKM2–PFKFB3 axis, which drives TAM M2 polarization through enhanced glycolytic reprogramming and PD-L1 upregulation, cooperates with hypoxia‐induced lactate accumulation and parallel pathways such as Wnt signaling to sustain an immunosuppressive milieu. By leveraging advanced nanocarrier systems for targeted delivery of PKM2 inhibitors (or PKM2‐siRNA) and modulators of PFKFB3 activity, we anticipate a reprogramming of TAMs toward a proinflammatory M1 phenotype. This metabolic and immunologic shift is expected to potentiate CD8+ T cell responses and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapies to achieve improved tumor control in HCC. Herein, we integrate the original mechanistic insights with contemporary technological strategies to address the complexity of the tumor microenvironment and enhance the therapeutic index of immunomodulatory interventions.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis focused on targeting the exosomal PKM2–PFKFB3 axis to reprogram TAMs and improve ICB efficacy in HCC. The revised version retains this core mechanism but explicitly integrates additional tumor microenvironment factors such as hypoxia-induced lactate accumulation and Wnt signaling, which are established as contributors to M2 polarization. Furthermore, the updated hypothesis proposes the use of contemporary nanocarrier technologies (e.g., siRNA delivery and CRISPR-based modulation) for precise and effective targeting of the PKM2–PFKFB3 axis. Each step of the original causal chain is maintained and expanded: from exosomal PKM2 release, its uptake by Kupffer cells/macrophages, PFKFB3-driven glycolysis, and subsequent upregulation of PD-L1 leading to M2 polarization, to the reversal mechanism that reactivates CD8+ T cell function and tumor suppression.
